about: Todos os comandos do QEMU: 'tools' são as ferramentas que não precisam da VM ligada (qemu-img, qemu-io, qemu-system-* -machine help…); 'hmp' são os comandos do monitor (digitados como estão, ex.: info registers); 'qmp' são os comandos do protocolo de máquina, enviados como JSON {"execute": nome, "arguments": {...}}; 'qmp_events' são os eventos que o QEMU envia. Gerado por tools/gen_qemu_catalog.py a partir do QEMU instalado e dos comentários do QAPI.

hmp.name: drive_backup
hmp.description: initiates a point-in-time copy for a device. The device's contents are copied to the new image file, excluding data that is written after the command is started. The -n flag requests QEMU to reuse the image found in new-image-file, instead of recreating it from scratch. The -f flag requests QEMU to copy the whole disk, so that the result does not need a backing file. The -c flag requests QEMU to compress backup data (if the target format supports it).

hmp.name: drive_mirror
hmp.description: initiates live storage migration for a device. The device's contents are copied to the new image file, including data that is written after the command is started. The -n flag requests QEMU to reuse the image found in new-image-file, instead of recreating it from scratch. The -f flag requests QEMU to copy the whole disk, so that the result does not need a backing file.

qmp.name: block-commit
qmp.description: Live commit of data from overlay image nodes into backing nodes - i.e., writes data between 'top' and 'base' into 'base'.

arguments.name: job-id
arguments.description: identifier for the newly-created block job. If omitted, the device name will be used. (Since 2.7)

arguments.name: device
arguments.description: the device name or node-name of a root node

arguments.name: base-node
arguments.description: The node name of the backing image to write data into. If not specified, this is the deepest backing image. (since: 3.1)

arguments.name: base
arguments.description: Same as @base-node, except that it is a file name rather than a node name. This must be the exact filename string that was used to open the node; other strings, even if addressing the same file, are not accepted

arguments.name: top-node
arguments.description: The node name of the backing image within the image chain which contains the topmost data to be committed down. If not specified, this is the active layer. (since: 3.1)

arguments.name: top
arguments.description: Same as @top-node, except that it is a file name rather than a node name. This must be the exact filename string that was used to open the node; other strings, even if addressing the same file, are not accepted

arguments.name: backing-file
arguments.description: The backing file string to write into the overlay image of 'top'. If 'top' does not have an overlay image, or if 'top' is in use by a writer, specifying a backing file string is an error.

arguments.name: backing-mask-protocol
arguments.description: If true, replace any protocol mentioned in the 'backing file format' with 'raw', rather than storing the protocol name as the backing format. Can be used even when no image header will be updated (default false; since 9.0).

arguments.name: speed
arguments.description: the maximum speed, in bytes per second

arguments.name: on-error
arguments.description: the action to take on an error. 'ignore' means that the request should be retried. (default: report; since: 5.0)

arguments.name: filter-node-name
arguments.description: the node name that should be assigned to the filter driver that the commit job inserts into the graph above @top. If this option is not given, a node name is autogenerated. (Since: 2.9)

arguments.name: auto-finalize
arguments.description: When false, this job will wait in a PENDING state after it has finished its work, waiting for `job-finalize` before making any block graph changes. When true, this job will automatically perform its abort or commit actions. Defaults to true. (Since 3.1)

arguments.name: auto-dismiss
arguments.description: When false, this job will wait in a CONCLUDED state after it has completely ceased all work, and awaits `job-dismiss`. When true, this job will automatically disappear without user intervention. Defaults to true. (Since 3.1)

qmp.name: block-dirty-bitmap-add
qmp.description: Create a dirty bitmap with a name on the node, and start tracking the writes.

arguments.name: node
arguments.description: name of device/node which the bitmap is tracking

arguments.name: name
arguments.description: name of the dirty bitmap (must be less than 1024 bytes)

arguments.name: granularity
arguments.description: the bitmap granularity, default is 64k for `block-dirty-bitmap-add`

arguments.name: persistent
arguments.description: the bitmap is persistent, i.e. it will be saved to the corresponding block device image file on its close. For now only Qcow2 disks support persistent bitmaps. Default is false for `block-dirty-bitmap-add`. (Since: 2.10)

arguments.name: disabled
arguments.description: the bitmap is created in the disabled state, which means that it will not track drive changes. The bitmap may be enabled with `block-dirty-bitmap-enable`. Default is false. (Since: 4.0)

qmp.name: block-dirty-bitmap-clear
qmp.description: Clear (reset) a dirty bitmap on the device, so that an incremental backup from this point in time forward will only backup clusters modified after this clear operation.

arguments.name: id

arguments.name: discard
arguments.description: discard-related options (default: ignore)

arguments.name: cache
arguments.description: cache-related options

arguments.name: active

qmp.name: blockdev-backup
qmp.description: Start a point-in-time copy of a block device to a new destination. The status of ongoing `blockdev-backup` operations can be checked with `query-block-jobs` where the `BlockJobInfo`.type field has the value 'backup'. The operation can be stopped before it has completed using the `job-cancel` or `block-job-cancel` command.

arguments.name: job-id
arguments.description: identifier for the newly-created block job. If omitted, the device name will be used. (Since 2.7)

arguments.name: device
arguments.description: the device name or node-name of a root node which should be copied.

arguments.name: sync
arguments.description: what parts of the disk image should be copied to the destination (all the disk, only the sectors allocated in the topmost image, from a dirty bitmap, or only new I/O).

arguments.name: speed
arguments.description: the maximum speed, in bytes per second. The default is 0, for unlimited.

arguments.name: bitmap
arguments.description: The name of a dirty bitmap to use. Must be present if sync is "bitmap" or "incremental". Can be present if sync is "full" or "top". Must not be present otherwise. (Since 2.4 (`drive-backup`), 3.1 (`blockdev-backup`))

arguments.name: bitmap-mode
arguments.description: Specifies the type of data the bitmap should contain after the operation concludes. Must be present if a bitmap was provided, must **not** be present otherwise. (Since 4.2)

arguments.name: compress
arguments.description: true to compress data, if the target format supports it. (default: false) (since 2.8)

arguments.name: on-source-error
arguments.description: the action to take on an error on the source, default 'report'. 'stop' and 'enospc' can only be used if the block device supports io-status (see `BlockInfo`).

arguments.name: on-target-error
arguments.description: the action to take on an error on the target, default 'report' (no limitations, since this applies to a different block device than @device).

arguments.name: on-cbw-error
arguments.description: policy defining behavior on I/O errors in copy-before-write jobs; defaults to break-guest-write. (Since 10.1)

arguments.name: auto-finalize
arguments.description: When false, this job will wait in a PENDING state after it has finished its work, waiting for `job-finalize` before making any block graph changes. When true, this job will automatically perform its abort or commit actions. Defaults to true. (Since 2.12)

arguments.name: auto-dismiss
arguments.description: When false, this job will wait in a CONCLUDED state after it has completely ceased all work, and awaits `job-dismiss`. When true, this job will automatically disappear without user intervention. Defaults to true. (Since 2.12)

arguments.name: filter-node-name
arguments.description: the node name that should be assigned to the filter driver that the backup job inserts into the graph above node specified by @drive. If this option is not given, a node name is autogenerated. (Since: 4.2)

arguments.name: discard-source
arguments.description: Discard blocks on source which have already been copied to the target. (Since 9.1)

arguments.name: x-perf
arguments.description: Performance options. (Since 6.0)

arguments.name: target
arguments.description: the device name or node-name of the backup target node.

arguments.name: device
arguments.description: Block device name

arguments.name: id

arguments.description: The name or QOM path of the guest device (since: 2.8)

arguments.name: job-id
arguments.description: Identifier for the newly created job.

arguments.name: options
arguments.description: Options for the image creation.

qmp.name: blockdev-del

arguments.name: sync
arguments.description: what parts of the disk image should be copied to the destination (all the disk, only the sectors allocated in the topmost image, or only new I/O).

arguments.name: speed

arguments.name: on-source-error
arguments.description: the action to take on an error on the source, default 'report'. 'stop' and 'enospc' can only be used if the block device supports io-status (see `BlockInfo`).

arguments.name: on-target-error
arguments.description: the action to take on an error on the target, default 'report' (no limitations, since this applies to a different block device than @device).

arguments.name: filter-node-name
arguments.description: the node name that should be assigned to the filter driver that the mirror job inserts into the graph above @device. If this option is not given, a node name is autogenerated. (Since: 2.9)

arguments.name: copy-mode
arguments.description: when to copy data to the destination; defaults to 'background' (Since: 3.0)

arguments.name: auto-finalize
arguments.description: When false, this job will wait in a PENDING state after it has finished its work, waiting for `job-finalize` before making any block graph changes. When true, this job will automatically perform its abort or commit actions. Defaults to true. (Since 3.1)

arguments.name: auto-dismiss
arguments.description: When false, this job will wait in a CONCLUDED state after it has completely ceased all work, and awaits `job-dismiss`. When true, this job will automatically disappear without user intervention. Defaults to true. (Since 3.1)

arguments.description: time period for which dirty page rate is calculated. By default it is specified in seconds, but the unit can be set explicitly with @calc-time-unit. Note that larger @calc-time values will typically result in smaller dirty page rates because page dirtying is a one-time event. Once some page is counted as dirty during @calc-time period, further writes to this page will not increase dirty page rate anymore.

arguments.name: calc-time-unit
arguments.description: time unit in which @calc-time is specified. By default it is seconds. (Since 8.2)

arguments.name: sample-pages
arguments.description: number of sampled pages per each GiB of guest memory. Default value is 512. For 4KiB guest pages this corresponds to sampling ratio of 0.2%. This argument is used only in page sampling mode. (Since 6.1)

arguments.name: mode
arguments.description: mechanism for tracking dirty pages. Default value is 'page-sampling'. Others are 'dirty-bitmap' and 'dirty-ring'. (Since 6.1)

qmp.name: cancel-vcpu-dirty-limit
qmp.description: Cancel the upper limit of dirty page rate for virtual CPUs.

arguments.name: cpu-index
arguments.description: index of a virtual CPU, default is all.

qmp.name: change-backing-file
qmp.description: Change the backing file in the image file metadata. The new backing file string is written into the image file metadata, and the QEMU internal strings are updated.

arguments.name: device
arguments.description: The device name or node-name of the root node that owns image-node-name.

arguments.name: image-node-name
arguments.description: The name of the block driver state node of the image to modify. The "device" argument is used to verify "image-node-name" is in the chain described by "device".

qmp.name: drive-backup
qmp.description: Start a point-in-time copy of a block device to a new destination. The status of ongoing `drive-backup` operations can be checked with `query-block-jobs` where the `BlockJobInfo`.type field has the value 'backup'. The operation can be stopped before it has completed using the `job-cancel` or `block-job-cancel` command.

arguments.name: job-id
arguments.description: identifier for the newly-created block job. If omitted, the device name will be used. (Since 2.7)

arguments.name: device
arguments.description: the device name or node-name of a root node which should be copied.

arguments.name: sync
arguments.description: what parts of the disk image should be copied to the destination (all the disk, only the sectors allocated in the topmost image, from a dirty bitmap, or only new I/O).

arguments.name: speed
arguments.description: the maximum speed, in bytes per second. The default is 0, for unlimited.

arguments.name: bitmap
arguments.description: The name of a dirty bitmap to use. Must be present if sync is "bitmap" or "incremental". Can be present if sync is "full" or "top". Must not be present otherwise. (Since 2.4 (`drive-backup`), 3.1 (`blockdev-backup`))

arguments.name: bitmap-mode
arguments.description: Specifies the type of data the bitmap should contain after the operation concludes. Must be present if a bitmap was provided, must **not** be present otherwise. (Since 4.2)

arguments.name: compress
arguments.description: true to compress data, if the target format supports it. (default: false) (since 2.8)

arguments.name: on-source-error
arguments.description: the action to take on an error on the source, default 'report'. 'stop' and 'enospc' can only be used if the block device supports io-status (see `BlockInfo`).

arguments.name: on-target-error
arguments.description: the action to take on an error on the target, default 'report' (no limitations, since this applies to a different block device than @device).

arguments.name: on-cbw-error
arguments.description: policy defining behavior on I/O errors in copy-before-write jobs; defaults to break-guest-write. (Since 10.1)

arguments.description: When false, this job will wait in a PENDING state after it has finished its work, waiting for `job-finalize` before making any block graph changes. When true, this job will automatically perform its abort or commit actions. Defaults to true. (Since 2.12)

arguments.name: auto-dismiss
arguments.description: When false, this job will wait in a CONCLUDED state after it has completely ceased all work, and awaits `job-dismiss`. When true, this job will automatically disappear without user intervention. Defaults to true. (Since 2.12)

arguments.name: filter-node-name
arguments.description: the node name that should be assigned to the filter driver that the backup job inserts into the graph above node specified by @drive. If this option is not given, a node name is autogenerated. (Since: 4.2)

arguments.name: discard-source
arguments.description: Discard blocks on source which have already been copied to the target. (Since 9.1)

arguments.name: x-perf
arguments.description: Performance options. (Since 6.0)

arguments.name: target
arguments.description: the target of the new image. If the file exists, or if it is a device, the existing file/device will be used as the new destination. If it does not exist, a new file will be created.

arguments.name: format
arguments.description: the format of the new destination, default is to probe if @mode is 'existing', else the format of the source

arguments.name: mode
arguments.description: whether and how QEMU should create a new image, default is 'absolute-paths'.

If the file exists, or if it is a device, it will be used as the new destination for writes. If it does not exist, a new file will be created. @format specifies the format of the mirror image, default is to probe if mode='existing', else the format of the source.

arguments.description: The ratio of bytes_dirty_period and bytes_xfer_period to trigger throttling. It is expressed as percentage. The default value is 50. (Since 5.0)

arguments.name: cpu-throttle-initial
arguments.description: Initial percentage of time guest cpus are throttled when migration auto-converge is activated. The default value is 20. (Since 2.7)

arguments.description: throttle percentage increase each time auto-converge detects that migration is not making progress. The default value is 10. (Since 2.7)

arguments.name: cpu-throttle-tailslow
arguments.description: Make CPU throttling slower at tail stage. At the tail stage of throttling, the Guest is very sensitive to CPU percentage while the @cpu-throttle -increment is excessive usually at tail stage. If this parameter is true, we will compute the ideal CPU percentage used by the Guest, which may exactly make the dirty rate match the dirty rate threshold. Then we will choose a smaller throttle increment between the one specified by @cpu-throttle-increment and the one generated by ideal CPU percentage. Therefore, it is compatible to traditional throttling, meanwhile the throttle increment won't be excessive at tail stage. The default value is false. (Since 5.1)

arguments.name: tls-creds
arguments.description: ID of the 'tls-creds' object that provides credentials for establishing a TLS connection over the migration data channel. On the outgoing side of the migration, the credentials must be for a 'client' endpoint, while for the incoming side the credentials must be for a 'server' endpoint. Setting this to a non-empty string enables TLS for all migrations. An empty string means that QEMU will use plain text mode for migration, rather than TLS. This is the default. (Since 2.7)

A non-empty value is required when using x509 based TLS credentials and the migration URI does not include a hostname, such as fd: or exec: based migration. (Since 2.7)

This object is only resolved at time of use, so can be deleted and recreated on the fly while the migration server is active. If missing, it will default to denying access (Since 4.0)

arguments.name: max-bandwidth
arguments.description: maximum speed for migration, in bytes per second. (Since 2.8)

arguments.name: avail-switchover-bandwidth
arguments.description: to set the available bandwidth that migration can use during switchover phase, in bytes per second. **Note:** this does not limit the bandwidth during switchover, but only for calculations when making decisions to switch over. By default, this value is zero, which means QEMU will estimate the bandwidth automatically. This can be set when the estimated value is not accurate, while the user is able to guarantee such bandwidth is available when switching over. When specified correctly, this can make the switchover decision much more accurate. (Since 8.2)

arguments.name: downtime-limit
arguments.description: set maximum tolerated downtime for migration. maximum downtime in milliseconds (Since 2.8)

arguments.name: x-checkpoint-delay
arguments.description: The delay time (in ms) between two COLO checkpoints in periodic mode. (Since 2.8)

arguments.description: Which compression method to use. Defaults to none. (Since 5.0)

arguments.name: multifd-zlib-level
arguments.description: Set the compression level to be used in live migration, the compression level is an integer between 0 and 9, where 0 means no compression, 1 means the best compression speed, and 9 means best compression ratio which will consume more CPU. Defaults to 1. (Since 5.0)

arguments.name: multifd-qatzip-level
arguments.description: Set the compression level to be used in live migration. The level is an integer between 1 and 9, where 1 means the best compression speed, and 9 means the best compression ratio which will consume more CPU. Defaults to 1. (Since 9.2)

arguments.name: multifd-zstd-level
arguments.description: Set the compression level to be used in live migration, the compression level is an integer between 0 and 20, where 0 means no compression, 1 means the best compression speed, and 20 means best compression ratio which will consume more CPU. Defaults to 1. (Since 5.0)

arguments.name: block-bitmap-mapping
arguments.description: Maps block nodes and bitmaps on them to aliases for the purpose of dirty bitmap migration. Such aliases may for example be the corresponding names on the opposite site. The mapping must be one-to-one, but not necessarily complete: On the source, unmapped bitmaps and all bitmaps on unmapped nodes will be ignored. On the destination, encountering an unmapped alias in the incoming migration stream will result in a report, and all further bitmap migration data will then be discarded. Note that the destination does not know about bitmaps it does not receive, so there is no limitation or requirement regarding the number of bitmaps received, or how they are named, or on which nodes they are placed. By default (when this parameter has never been set), bitmap names are mapped to themselves. Nodes are mapped to their block device name if there is one, and to their node name otherwise. (Since 5.2)

qmp_events.description: Emitted when a disk image is being marked corrupt. The image can be identified by its device or node name. The 'device' field is always present for compatibility reasons, but it can be empty ("") if the image does not have a device name associated.

data.name: size
data.description: if the corruption resulted from an image access, this is the access size
